target_segments.source_text: "Gust from your left—three seconds—dip and hold!" Nisa's voice cracked across the air, and Arda dipped, held, and felt the wind pass a hand's width above his wing.
Arda brought the glider in at an angle, half-flying and half-falling, and a root caught the skid and tilted him sideways.
"Line—now!" Nisa shouted, and Arda had the light expedition line off his harness and lashed to a stout trunk before he'd finished thinking about it.
It was nothing like any pattern he'd ever seen.
Somewhere behind them, back past the shore, the corridor they'd flown through was, presumably, still open.
"I'll be back soon; we want to be off this island before the light fades.
"We have to hurry; the wind is picking up," he said.

They came down through the mist-filled trees at a dead run and found the great root span still hooked to its far anchor, its near anchors torn loose, thrashing in the wind above a drop into the cloud sea.
He anchored it to the last living trunk on his side, swung the free end across the gap, and Nisa caught it and hauled herself across hand over hand while the wind tried to peel her off.
He got three-quarters of the way across before the trunk anchoring the bridge groaned.
The bridge was dropping, and the line tied to the falling span was still clipped to his harness, dragging him backward.
The bridge fell away beneath him into the cloud sea, and Arda lunged for the ledge where Nisa waited. She leaned out and hauled; his hand found her wrist, and her grip found him.
Their gliders still lay on the shore, Arda's tilted where it had been left.
He knew only that it had been real, and that the proof was safely tucked away.
